newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi's Banda charged with $9 million fraud.
newsitem.headline: Malawi's Banda charged with $9 million fraud.

text.p: Malawi's former "life president" Kamuzu Banda, who ruled the country with an iron fist for three decades until 1994, was charged in the High Court on Friday with fraud involving more than $9 million.
Banda, believed to be 96-years-old, did not appear in court because of old age and ill health.

Heavily armed military police surrounded the court and patrolled the two km (one mile) route to Banda's Mudi residence as hundreds of supporters from his main opposition Malawi Congress Party demonstrated outside the court building.

Banda is charged together with his former aide John Tembo, Banda's long-time companion Cecilia Kadzamira, and former finance minister Louis Chimango who appeared on Friday in a Blantyre magistrate's court.
The case was transferred to the High Court for trial on a date still to be set.
They are charged with allegedly abusing public funds between 1982 and 1996 and converting trust property to Banda's classical grammar school, the Kamazu Academy. "They (defence lawyers)
requested if he could be excused not to appear in this court. I indicated I would not insist that he appears in this court," prosecutor Kamudoni Nyasulu told Reuters.
In 1995 Banda stood trial with Tembo and Kadzamira on charges of ordering the assassination of four political opponents in 1983. They were acquitted by the High Court.
Banda became president of Malawi in 1966 and proclaimed himself president for life in 1971, crushing all dissent. He lost power to Bakili Muluzi in democratic polls in 1994.
